Define a Field for an LLM Coding Schema

Source: R/schema.R
schema_field.Rd

Specifies the expected type, bounds, allowed levels, nullability, and requirement status for a single field in structured JSON LLM output.

Usage

schema_field(
  type = c("numeric", "integer", "factor", "enum", "logical", "character"),
  min = NULL,
  max = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  required = TRUE,
  nullable = FALSE,
  description = NULL
)

Arguments

type

Field type: one of "numeric", "integer", "factor", "enum", "logical", or "character". ("enum" is an alias for "factor".)

min

Optional numeric lower bound (for "numeric" or "integer").

max

Optional numeric upper bound (for "numeric" or "integer").

levels

Character vector of allowed category labels (required when type is "factor" or "enum").

required

Logical; whether the field must be present in every parsed JSON payload. Default TRUE.

nullable

Logical; whether JSON null / NA is allowed. Default FALSE.

description

Optional character description embedded in JSON Schema prompts and structured-output specifications.

Value

An object of class "llm_schema_field".

Examples

schema_field("numeric", min = 1, max = 7, description = "Distress rating")
#> $type
#> [1] "numeric"
#> 
#> $min
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $max
#> [1] 7
#> 
#> $levels
#> NULL
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $nullable
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $description
#> [1] "Distress rating"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "llm_schema_field"
schema_field("factor", levels = c("low", "medium", "high"))
#> $type
#> [1] "factor"
#> 
#> $min
#> NULL
#> 
#> $max
#> NULL
#> 
#> $levels
#> [1] "low"    "medium" "high"  
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $nullable
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $description
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "llm_schema_field"
